decision_titles: Draft regional housing needs assessment and South Burlington action plan
plain_text:
Page 1 
Housing Committee 
October 21, 2026  
 
The South Burlington Housing Committee was called to order at 6:00 PM on October 21  in 
City Hall, 180 Market Street and via Zoom.  
 
Committee members present included co-Chairs Nora Senecal and Meghan Tedder, then 
members Vince Bolduc, Tasos Lois, Dawn Philibert. Mona Tolba and Sandy Dooley were 
on-line. 
 
Others present: Kelsey Peterson (Senior City Planner),  Elizabeth Fitzgerald, (designated 
representative from the City Council) and Ryan Doyle was present on line as a members of 
the public.  
 
Minutes from the last meeting were approved.  
 
Staff report and discussion: Kelsey included in tonight’s minutes two documents that we 
were to consider for this meeting.  As she put it: “One is the draft Request for Proposals 
(RFP) for the Housing Needs Assessment being conducted by the Chittenden County 
Regional Planning Commission (CCRPC). The second is the draft sub-task for the RFP that 
specifically outlines the proposed South Burlington Housing Action Plan.” The latter is part 
and parcel of the Chittenden Country Regional Needs Assessment, referenced on the third 
and last page of the CCRPC RFP. In a sense, our Housing Action Plan would flow directly 
from the regional assessment and could become something of a pilot that could be used 
in the larger needs assessment for other communities if ours is successful. The SB Action 
Plan would add to the total cost, but would be less than if it were done independently.   
 
The Housing Committee could find no major gaps in the Regional Needs Assessment RFP 
as presented, nor in the SB aspect of the RFP which address deficits in the housing needs 
of our community. Some appreciated the recognition of the imbalance in our city’s 
housing stock and the goal of defining “…the characteristics of a healthy, balanced and

economically stable regional community.” Various members of our committee also felt 
that it would help to add explicit encouragements to higher density developments and 
smaller living units than have characterized SB in the recent past. The preservation of 
natural resources is prominent in recent City action, but the relatively modest 
construction of “missing middle” is also apparent and referenced in the draft Act Plan.  
 
The Committee adjourned at 8:00. 
Respectfully submitted, 
Vince Bolduc, Secretary
